runs.research_summary: Ran targeted live searches for the November 9–13 earnings calendar, recent guidance changes, earnings reactions, industrial/logistics opportunities, healthcare, power, semiconductor suppliers and NYSE American issuers. Opened issuer releases, an SEC operating filing, historical observations and timestamped reporting. Coverage was selective, not exhaustive. Compared smaller-company leads including REI and CECO, mid-sized industrial GXO, and larger technology/travel issuers; share price was not used as a market-cap proxy. ABNB's fresh operating acceleration plus a documented earnings response produced the clearest, though modest, weekly directional case. GXO had 6.4% organic growth but flat adjusted EBITDA, lower cash generation and its investor day outside the window. CSCO and AMAT have within-window earnings timing, but timing alone did not establish favorable surprises; CSCO's historical growth did not resolve expectations. REI's approximately $1.11 historical close fails the $5 floor. CECO's issuer site flagged a listing transfer, leaving exchange eligibility unresolved. GFS/VTRS/BWXT/VST were discovery leads without a stronger fully corroborated weekly setup; DKNG's reported guidance cut and CRWV's event risk weakened their comparisons. Submitted one finalist rather than force three. Two primary sources support ABNB. Historical daily data show more than 20 sessions and substantial volume, but no fresh cutoff-valid engine quote exists. Undated historical pages have null publication timestamps: only dated observations preceding cutoff are used, and retrospective revision remains possible. No subsequent earnings outcomes or unverified same-day previews were used. All allocation and execution checks remain binding.

runs.research_summary: Independently searched November 6 gainers, unusual volume, weekly performance and recent earnings across Nasdaq, NYSE and NYSE American, then opened issuer/SEC disclosures and public history. Discovery included smaller-company opportunities alongside larger issuers across travel, defense, solar infrastructure, photonics, uranium, software and semiconductors; this was not exhaustive market coverage or a verified market-cap ranking. ABNB was the strongest adequately documented finalist. KRMN had strong reported growth but a 42.13% session jump created substantially greater extension risk. ARRY's merger announcement complicated a standalone continuation forecast. COHR's rebound followed a larger earnings-session decline and did not restore its pre-release close. UEC's rebound remained within a pronounced monthly decline. THM and GOGO were below $5 in discovery observations; AMD's $449.04 reference exceeded the approximately $396.32 ticker cap even for one share. APP/RKLB were discovery comparisons without sufficient follow-up verification to propose; DKNG showed adverse earnings momentum. ABNB's positive weekly direction contrasted with reported S&P 500 and Nasdaq weekly declines, but sector-relative strength was not independently quantified. Opened history establishes more than 20 completed ABNB sessions, with displayed October daily volumes exceeding one million; another provider reports a 3.76 million 30-day average. Volume totals differ across providers, so no exact relative-volume statistic is asserted. November 9's partial bar is intraday, not a completed close. Separate raw-close and adjusted-close columns agree in the opened older history; ChartExchange's adjustment methodology was not established. No ATR, realized-volatility estimate or moving-average indicator was invented. Undated dynamic pages are assigned null publication timestamps; only explicitly dated observations before the cutoff were used. Search snippets sometimes differed from opened pages, and Yahoo history was rate-limited. Fresh backend prices, liquidity, corporate actions and affordability still require validation. Estimates are subjective and conditional on entry price; no other researcher's findings were received.
